6.7.6.5 Program Outcome ​

Typical effects are as follows:

FunctionDescriptionReturn Value Example
Distance detectionRead ultrasonic distance measurement and return the millimeter valuedistance = 235
Linkage promptCan combine with the large model to generate voice broadcasting or action suggestionsThere is an obstacle about 23.5 centimeters ahead

6.7.6.6 Program Analysis ​

  1. Ultrasonic distance measurement is completed by sonar_get_distance_mm. The function reads the basic distance value from i2csonar.getDistance, and then multiplies it by 10 to convert it to millimeters. Therefore, the unit of the returned distance here is millimeter.
python
def sonar_get_distance_mm():
    with i2c_lock:
        value = i2csonar.getDistance()
    return int(value * 10)
  1. The i2c_lock is used here because the ultrasonic sensor, RGB lights, and large AI model module share the same I2C bus. When multiple threads access the bus simultaneously, data conflicts can easily occur.
python
with i2c_lock:
    value = i2csonar.getDistance()
  1. When the large model queries the distance, the message passes through _parse_payload first. As long as status_name appears in the JSON, the program identifies it as a status type command, and then passes it to the status query logic for processing.
python
status_name = self._find_key(obj, "status_name")
if status_name is not None:
    return {"type": "status", "status_name": str(status_name)}
  1. Reading the distance is completed in get_llm_status_pairs. The program first converts status_name to lowercase, checks if the keyword distance is inside, and then reads the current distance upon matching.
python
if "distance" in name:
    return [["distance", str(sonar_get_distance_mm())]]
  1. The return value is not a single integer, but is organized into a list of key-value pairs like [["distance", "value"]] according to the protocol, so as to maintain the same format as other status items such as battery level, mode, and posture.
python
return [["distance", str(sonar_get_distance_mm())]]
  1. When handle_llm_command encounters a status type command, it unifiedly calls send_status to send the result back to the module. The status query returns status data instead of action_finish.
python
elif cmd_type == "status":
    pairs = get_llm_status_pairs(cmd.get("status_name", ""))
    llm_bridge.send_status(pairs)
  1. Obstacle detection itself belongs to status query. Therefore, no new tool is defined. Instead, the self.robot.get_status interface is reused directly. Querying distance, battery level, mode, and posture all share the same entry.
python
self.tool_status = {
    "tool_name": "self.robot.get_status",
    "params": [["status_name", "string"]],
    "block": "true",
    "return": "true",
}
  1. In addition to distance, the same status query logic also supports battery, running_mode, and Bodystate. Among them, running_mode returns string mode names: normal, avoid, and follow.
python
if "battery" in name:
    return [["battery", str(battery_volt)]]
if "running_mode" in name:
    return [["running_mode", MODE_CODE_TO_NAME.get(status_func, "normal")]]
if "bodystate" in name:
    return [["Bodystate", str(body_state)]]

6.7.7 Smart Traffic Driving ​

6.7.7.1 Project Introduction ​

This part mainly realizes line following driving through the ESP32-S3 vision module paired with the Tonybot robot, and uses the chest large AI model module to identify traffic lights to control the robot to stop or proceed.

6.7.7.2 Implementation Flow ​

6.7.7.3 Module Description ​

  • Large AI Model Module

The large AI model module has a built-in ESP32-S3 high-performance chip and integrates a 2-megapixel high-definition camera, microphone, high-definition display screen, speaker, and CI1302 voice recognition chip. It deeply integrates various models such as language, voice, and vision.

  • ESP32-S3 Vision Module

The ESP32-S3 camera module is a cost-effective AI vision solution. It is developed based on the ESP32-S3 high-performance chip and supports Wi-Fi video streaming, color recognition, face recognition, and line following recognition. Integrating a 2-megapixel camera, this module uses industrial-grade manufacturing processes, supports C/C++ programming, and is equipped with a Type-C serial port, I2C interface, and customized buttons to provide convenient hardware interaction interfaces.

6.7.7.4 Program Download ​

NOTE

Before downloading the program, ensure that the serial port driver has been installed.

  1. Connect Tonybot to the computer using a Type-C data cable.
  1. Open the Hiwonder Python Editor software.
  1. Drag 02 Source Code\02 Smart Traffic Driving Program\main.py under the same directory into the Hiwonder Python Editor. Note that this is only effective when dragged into the red box area.
  1. Click the connection button on the menu bar. After a successful connection, the icon will turn green .
  2. After connecting successfully, click the download button on the menu bar to download the program into Tonybot, and wait for the message box below to prompt that the download is complete.

6.7.7.5 Program Outcome ​

After powering on, the program initializes the robot and I2C peripherals and waits for WonderLLM at address 0x55 to be ready. Then the robot enters the line following mode, continuously reading the line position from the camera to control the robot to move straight or turn for line following. When the yellow line trigger point is recognized and the blue block condition is satisfied, the robot switches to the waiting stage. In this stage, the robot repeatedly sends camera vision requests to WonderLLM and polls the returned results. When the recognition result indicates a green light with vision equal to true, the robot executes the through action group. After completion, it returns to the initial posture and re-enters line following, with the entire process running in a loop.

6.7.7.6 Program Analysis ​

  1. The program imports dependencies first upon startup, and uses ticks_ms and ticks_diff for timing to ensure stable timing logic under MicroPython.
python
import json
import Hiwonder
import Hiwonder_IIC
import time

def _elapsed_ms(start_ticks):
    return time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), start_ticks)

def _now_ticks():
    return time.ticks_ms()
  1. Initialize I2C, robot, ultrasonic sensor, and camera objects. The I2C bus works preferentially at a rate of 400k and falls back if not supported. Configure the I2C address of WonderLLM and the initialization waiting parameters.
python
try:
    iic = Hiwonder_IIC.IIC(1, 23, 22, 400000)
except Exception:
    iic = Hiwonder_IIC.IIC()

tony = Hiwonder.Tonybot()
sonar = Hiwonder_IIC.I2CSonar(iic)
cam = Hiwonder_IIC.ESP32S3Cam(iic)

WONDERLLM_ADDR = 0x55
_LLM_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000
_LLM_INIT_POLL_MS = 500
  1. Define action group numbers, line following thresholds, and state machine stage constants. Subsequent line following, waiting, and through actions will branch based on these constants.
python
TURN_RIGHT = 66
TURN_LEFT = 65
GO_STRAIGHT = 63

LEFT_MIN = 240 // 2 - 40
RIGHT_MAX = 240 // 2 + 40

STAGE_LINETRACKING = 0
STAGE_WAITING = 1
STAGE_CUSTOM = 2
  1. After powering on, the robot executes the initialization posture and servo angles, sets initial state machine variables, and then prints start., indicating entry into the main process.
python
tony.runActionGroup(0, 1)
tony.attachHead()
tony.moveHeadAngle(90)
time.sleep_ms(2000)

print("start.")
stage = STAGE_LINETRACKING
tickstart1 = 0
tickstart2 = 0
  1. VISION_PROMPT is the prompt word for calling WonderLLM camera vision. last_vision_json_raw caches the most recently parsed {"vision":"true/false"}.
python
VISION_PROMPT = "Identify the front image. If there is a traffic light in front and it is green, return only true. Otherwise, return only false. Do not return any other information."
last_vision_json_raw = None
  1. body_follow represents line-following motion control. Based on whether the recognized line center x falls to the left or right of the threshold interval, it executes straight, left turn, or right turn action groups, using step as a simple state machine.
python
def body_follow(x):
    global step
    if not tony.isRunning():
        if LEFT_MIN < x < RIGHT_MAX:
            tony.runActionGroup(GO_STRAIGHT, 1)
        elif 0 < x < LEFT_MIN:
            tony.runActionGroup(TURN_LEFT, 2)
        else:
            tony.runActionGroup(TURN_RIGHT, 2)
  1. Read the black line block on channel 1 and the yellow line trigger block on channel 3 for line following using cam.read_color respectively, which are used for line following control and entering the waiting stage.
python
def read_black_block():
    result = cam.read_color(1)
    if result is not None and len(result) >= 4:
        return result[0] + result[2] // 2
    return None

def read_yellow_block():
    result = cam.read_color(3)
    if result is not None and len(result) >= 4:
        return result
    return None
  1. wonderllm_request_vision sends MCP requests such as tool_name=mcu.request and command=vision to WonderLLM via I2C to trigger the LLM to call the camera for recognition.
python
def wonderllm_request_vision(prompt):
    obj = {"tool_name": "mcu.request", "command": "vision", "params": prompt}
    raw = json.dumps(obj).encode("utf-8")
    iic.writeto(WONDERLLM_ADDR, raw)
  1. _parse_llm_header is used to parse the 8-byte packet header returned by WonderLLM. It is compatible with both 0xAA 0x55 and 0xAB variant formats to obtain information such as data_len, part_id, and part_num.
python
def _parse_llm_header(header):
    if header[0] == 0xAA and header[1] == 0x55:
        data_len = (header[2] << 8) | header[3]
        part_id = (header[5] << 8) | header[4]
        part_num = (header[7] << 8) | header[6]
        return (data_len, part_id, part_num, False)
  1. _wonderllm_read_one_payload reads all fragments of a message starting from part_id==1 and splices them into payload for subsequent parsing of vision JSON.
python
def _wonderllm_read_one_payload():
    header = iic.readfrom(WONDERLLM_ADDR, 8)
    data_len, part_id, part_num, is_ab_fmt = _parse_llm_header(header)
    buffer = []
    for i in range(part_num):
        body = iic.readfrom(WONDERLLM_ADDR, data_len + 1)
        buffer.append(body[:-1])
    return b"".join(buffer)
  1. wonderllm_poll_vision_result accumulates the multiple received payload into _llm_rx_buffer. After extracting the complete JSON, it parses the vision field, accepting only true, false, or boolean values, and updates last_vision_json_raw.
python
_llm_rx_buffer = b""

def wonderllm_poll_vision_result():
    global last_vision_json_raw, _llm_rx_buffer
    payload = _wonderllm_read_one_payload()
    _llm_rx_buffer += payload
    raw_str = _llm_rx_buffer.decode("utf-8").strip()
    candidate = raw_str[raw_str.find("{"): raw_str.rfind("}") + 1]
    obj = json.loads(candidate)
    if obj.get("vision") in (True, False, "true", "false"):
        last_vision_json_raw = candidate
  1. check_green_light_vision determines the green light only when vision is explicitly True or "true", which avoids misjudgment caused by long text or abnormal content.
python
def check_green_light_vision():
    if last_vision_json_raw is None:
        return False
    obj = json.loads(last_vision_json_raw)
    v = obj.get("vision")
    return (v is True) or (isinstance(v, str) and v.lower() == "true")
  1. Call wait_llm_ready to wait for WonderLLM initialization before the main loop starts. In the main loop, perform line following first, and enter the waiting stage to request vision immediately after recognizing the yellow line. During the waiting stage, request once every second and poll once every 50ms. After identifying the green light, execute the through action group and return to the line following loop.
python
wait_llm_ready()
while True:
    if stage == STAGE_LINETRACKING:
        x = read_black_block()
        if x is not None:
            body_follow(x)
        blue = read_yellow_block()
        if blue is not None and blue[1] >= 120:
            stage = STAGE_WAITING
            _llm_rx_buffer = b""
            last_vision_json_raw = None
            wonderllm_request_vision(VISION_PROMPT)

    elif stage == STAGE_WAITING:
        if _elapsed_ms(tickstart1) >= 1000:
            wonderllm_request_vision(VISION_PROMPT)
        if _elapsed_ms(tickstart2) >= 50:
            wonderllm_poll_vision_result()
            if check_green_light_vision():
                stage = STAGE_CUSTOM
                tony.runActionGroup(1, 4)

6.8 Large AI Model Offline Course ​

6.8.1 Introduction to Library Files and Registers ​

This section will analyze the library files related to the Tonybot AI body driving the large AI model module. The hw_esp32S3cam_ctl library is responsible for obtaining the face information and color recognition data detected by the large AI model module. This library consists of two files: hw_esp32S3cam_ctl.h and hw_esp32S3cam_ctl.cpp.

6.8.1.1 Library File Description ​

  • Member Function HW_ESP32S3CAM::begin
cpp
void HW_ESP32S3CAM::begin()
{
    Wire.setClock(100000);
    Wire.begin();
}

This function is used to initialize the I2C bus configuration, allowing instructions to be sent to and data to be received from the large AI model module through the bus later.

  • Low-Level Function Wire_Read_Data_Array
cpp
static int Wire_Read_Data_Array(uint8_t reg, 
                                uint8_t *val, 
                                uint16_t len)
{
    uint16_t i = 0;
    
    /* Indicate which register we want to read from */
    if (!Wire_Write_Byte(reg)) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    /* Read block data */
    Wire.requestFrom(ESP32S3_ADDR, len);
    while (Wire.available()) {
        if (i >= len) {
            return -1;
        }
        val[i] = Wire.read();
        i++;
    }   
    return i;
}
AttributeDetails
Function descriptionSend data to the large AI model module via the I2C bus
Parameter listreg, val, len
Return valueFalse: write failed, True: write succeeded
InstructionsCall HW_ESP32S3CAM::Init before using this function. This function is not used in subsequent development, so only a brief understanding is necessary.

Parameters and meanings:

  1. reg: The target memory address to write to in the large AI model module

  2. *val: The address of the data to be sent

  3. len: The length of the word to be sent

The Arduino primary device first sends the device address via the I2C bus, then sends the target memory address to the large AI model module, and finally sends the data byte by byte based on the word length. After that, Wire.endTransmission() is called to check whether the data is successfully sent. If the return value is 0, the data transmission is successful. Otherwise, it fails.

  • Low-Level Function Wire_Write_Byte
c
static bool Wire_Write_Byte(uint8_t val)
{
    Wire.beginTransmission(ESP32S3_ADDR);
    Wire.write(val);
    if( Wire.endTransmission() != 0 ) {
        return false;
    }
    return true;
}
AttributeDetails
Function descriptionConfirm the address of the data register to be read before reading data from the large AI model module
Parameter listval
Return valueFalse: transmission failed, True: transmission succeeded
InstructionsCall HW_ESP32S3CAM::Init before using this function. During data transmission or writing, the data register address for writing must also be confirmed with the secondary device. The same implementation statement of this function is also present inside Wire_Write_Data_Array().

Parameters and meanings:

val: The data content to be sent

The Arduino primary device directly sends the device address to the large AI model module and then sends one byte of data to the large AI model module. After that, Wire.endTransmission() is called to check whether the data is successfully sent. If the return value is 0, the data transmission is successful. Otherwise, it fails.

  • Low-Level Function Wire_Read_Data_Array
cpp
static int Wire_Read_Data_Array(uint8_t reg, 
                                uint8_t *val, 
                                uint16_t len)
{
    uint16_t i = 0;
    
    /* Indicate which register we want to read from */
    if (!Wire_Write_Byte(reg)) {
        return -1;
    }
    
    /* Read block data */
    Wire.requestFrom(ESP32S3_ADDR, len);
    while (Wire.available()) {
        if (i >= len) {
            return -1;
        }
        val[i] = Wire.read();
        i++;
    }   
    return i;
}
AttributeDetails
Function descriptionRead multi-byte data from the large AI model module via the I2C bus
Parameter listreg, val, len
Return value-1: Reading failed, other: successfully read data length
InstructionsCall HW_ESP32S3CAM::Init before using this function. Call Wire_Write_Byte to determine the read register address before using this function.

Parameters and meanings:

  1. reg: The data address to read from in the large AI model module

  2. *val: The address in the Arduino primary device used to store the received data

  3. len: The length of the word to read

The Arduino primary device first sends the read address to the large AI model module. If there is no response, -1 is returned, indicating that the connection to the large AI model module failed. Next, the word length is sent to the large AI model module. The data is read byte by byte through a while loop using the variable i and is stored in the val[] array. If the actual read length exceeds the requested word length during the reading process, -1 is returned to indicate reading failure. Finally, upon successful reading, i is returned, representing the actual read word length, which may be less than len.

  • Member Function HW_ESP32S3CAM::Face_Data_Receive
c
uint16_t HW_ESP32S3CAM::Face_Data_Receive(uint8_t *buf, uint8_t buf_len)
{
    return Wire_Read_Data_Array(FACE_DETECTION_REG, buf, buf_len);
}
AttributeDetails
Function descriptionRead the face detection results from the large AI model module
Parameter listReg, buf, buf_len
Return valueNone
InstructionsThis function is essentially a wrapper that directly calls Wire_Read_Data_Array. The physical meanings of the specific parameters are consistent with those in Wire_Read_Data_Array.

When implementing the color recognition and vision-based line following functions, the internal implementation of the functions is highly consistent with that of face recognition. Details are not repeated here. Review the source code and combine it with 6.8.1.2 Device Primary-Secondary Communication Principles (I2C Registers) below to understand the physical meaning of the information stored at each address in the functional registers of the large AI model module.

6.8.4.4 Program Analysis ​

  • Large AI Model Module
  1. image.ino imports header files related to Wi-Fi, camera, and LCD first. The network services and local display used for image transmission are all accessed from here.
c
#include <WiFi.h>
#include "camera_setting.h"
#include "lcd_display.h"
  1. The program defines the hotspot name, password, and static IP address in advance. This allows the video page to be opened directly via 192.168.5.1 after connecting to the hotspot of the module.
c
const char* ssid = "HW_ESP32S3CAM";
const char* password = "";

IPAddress local_ip(192, 168, 5, 1);
IPAddress gateway(192, 168, 1, 1);
IPAddress subnet(255, 255, 255, 0);
  1. startCameraServer() is implemented in app_httpd.cpp and is declared here first. xQueueAIFrame is used to transfer image frames between the camera acquisition task and the display task.
c
void startCameraServer();

static QueueHandle_t xQueueAIFrame = NULL;
  1. setup creates the image queue and registers the camera and LCD display modules at the very beginning. This allows the image to be displayed on the screen and transmitted to the web page.
cpp
xQueueAIFrame = xQueueCreate(3, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
register_camera(PIXFORMAT_RGB565, 4, xQueueAIFrame);
register_lcd_display(xQueueAIFrame, NULL, NULL, NULL, true);
  1. The program then switches the ESP32-S3 to AP mode, configures the static IP, and starts the hotspot. The video stream page can be accessed once a mobile phone or a computer is connected to this hotspot.
cpp
WiFi.mode(WIFI_AP);
if (!WiFi.softAPConfig(local_ip, gateway, subnet)) {
    Serial.println("Failed to configure IP");
}
WiFi.softAP(ssid, password, 6, false, 4);
WiFi.setSleep(false);
  1. After the hotspot starts successfully, setup continues to call startCameraServer() to start the web video streaming service, and finally prints the access URL to the serial port.
cpp
startCameraServer();

Serial.print("Camera Web Server Ready! Use 'http://");
Serial.print(WiFi.softAPIP());
Serial.println("' to connect");
  1. loop itself does not process specific tasks since image acquisition, display, and web transmission are already running continuously as background tasks. Therefore, only an idle delay is maintained here.
cpp
void loop() {
    delay(10000);
}
  1. The function actually responsible for acquiring images in camera_setting.c is task_process_handler(). It continuously reads frame data from the driver layer and then sends valid frames to the output queue.
c
static void task_process_handler(void *arg)
{
    int frame_count = 0;
    const int SKIP_FRAMES = 12;

    while (true)
    {
        camera_fb_t *frame = esp_camera_fb_get();
        if (frame)
        {
            frame_count++;
            if (frame_count > SKIP_FRAMES) {
                xQueueSend(xQueueFrameO, &frame, portMAX_DELAY);
            } else {
                esp_camera_fb_return(frame);
            }
        }
    }
}
  1. The first 12 frames are actively discarded to avoid the startup phase where exposure and white balance are unstable, reducing screen jitter and color distortion after startup.
c
const int SKIP_FRAMES = 12;

if (frame_count > SKIP_FRAMES) {
    xQueueSend(xQueueFrameO, &frame, portMAX_DELAY);
} else {
    esp_camera_fb_return(frame);
}
  1. In register_camera, the camera_config_t structure is assembled to configure data pins, clock pins, frame format, buffer location, and other parameters all at once.
c
camera_config_t config;
config.ledc_channel = LEDC_CHANNEL_0;
config.ledc_timer = LEDC_TIMER_0;
config.pin_d0 = Y2_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d1 = Y3_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d2 = Y4_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d3 = Y5_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d4 = Y6_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d5 = Y7_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d6 = Y8_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_d7 = Y9_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_xclk = XCLK_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_pclk = PCLK_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_vsync = VSYNC_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_href = HREF_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_sccb_sda = SIOD_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_sccb_scl = SIOC_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_pwdn = PWDN_GPIO_NUM;
config.pin_reset = RESET_GPIO_NUM;
config.frame_size = FRAMESIZE_240X240;
config.pixel_format = pixel_fromat;
config.grab_mode = CAMERA_GRAB_WHEN_EMPTY;
config.fb_location = CAMERA_FB_IN_PSRAM;
config.fb_count = fb_count;
  1. After configuration is completed, the program initializes the camera via esp_camera_init, fine-tunes mirroring, flipping, and saturation according to different sensor models, and finally creates the acquisition task.
c
esp_err_t err = esp_camera_init(&config);
if (err != ESP_OK) {
    ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Camera init failed with error 0x%x", err);
    return;
}

sensor_t *s = esp_camera_sensor_get();
if (s->id.PID == OV3660_PID || s->id.PID == OV2640_PID) {
    s->set_vflip(s, 1);
} else if (s->id.PID == GC0308_PID) {
    s->set_hmirror(s, 0);
}

xQueueFrameO = frame_o;
xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(task_process_handler, TAG, 3 * 1024, NULL, 2, NULL, 1);

6.8.5 Color Recognition ​

6.8.5.1 Project Introduction ​

This section introduces how to recognize colors by connecting to the large AI model module on the chest of Tonybot and control the RGB ultrasonic sensor on the head of the robot to synchronize its color with the recognized color.

6.8.5.2 Program Download ​

Refer to 6.8.3 Program Download of this chapter to learn how to download the program.

6.8.5.3 Program Outcome ​

When any of the three colors red, green, or blue is placed in front of the lens of the large AI model module on the chest of Tonybot, the RGB ultrasonic sensor on the head of Tonybot will change to the corresponding color.

6.8.5.4 Program Analysis ​

  • Large AI Model Module
  1. color_detection.ino imports the camera, color recognition, LCD, and I2C transmission modules first. The color recognition process is connected through these four components.
cpp
#include "camera_setting.h"
#include "color_detection.hpp"
#include "lcd_display.h"
#include "iic_data_send.hpp"
  1. A total of three sets of queues are created in the main program: the raw image input queue, the LCD display queue, and the I2C result queue. Images and recognition results are transmitted between different tasks through these queues.
cpp
static QueueHandle_t xQueueAIFrame = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueLCDFrame = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueIICData = NULL;
  1. In setup, queues are created first, followed by registering the camera, color recognition, LCD display, and I2C transmission modules sequentially. This connects image acquisition, recognition, display, and transmission.
cpp
xQueueAIFrame = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
xQueueLCDFrame = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
xQueueIICData = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(color_data_t *) * SEND_CLOLOR_NUM);

register_camera(PIXFORMAT_RGB565, 4, xQueueAIFrame);
register_color_detection(xQueueAIFrame, NULL, xQueueIICData, xQueueLCDFrame, false);
register_lcd_display(xQueueLCDFrame, NULL, NULL, NULL, true);
register_iic_data_send(xQueueIICData, NULL);
  1. The input, output, and result queue handles, as well as the global array color_data[4], are defined in color_detection.cpp. The recognition results for each color will be written here later.
cpp
static QueueHandle_t xQueueFrameI = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueEvent = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueFrameO = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueResult = NULL;

static bool gReturnFB = true;
color_data_t color_data[4];
  1. The color recognition thresholds are defined in std_color_info. Four colors including red, green, blue, and purple are registered by default, and subsequent recognition matches against these thresholds.
cpp
vector<color_info_t> std_color_info = {
    {{0, 67, 144, 255, 94, 255}, 64, "red"},
    {{69, 88, 144, 197, 108, 255}, 64, "green"},
    {{87, 186, 138, 255, 126, 254}, 64, "blue"},
    {{125, 155, 70, 255, 90, 255}, 64, "purple"}
};
  1. The function get_color_detection_result selects the block with the largest area among multiple detected color blocks of the same color, and writes the center point, width, and height into color_data.
cpp
if (results[i].area > g_max_color_area)
{
    dl::image::draw_hollow_rectangle(image_ptr, image_height, image_width,
                                        results[i].box[0],
                                        results[i].box[1],
                                        results[i].box[2],
                                        results[i].box[3],
                                        color);
    g_max_color_area= results[i].area;
    g_max_color_column_index = i;
}

case COLOR_RED:
  color_data[0].id = 1;
  color_data[0].center_x = (uint8_t)results[g_max_color_column_index].center[0];
  color_data[0].center_y = (uint8_t)results[g_max_color_column_index].center[1];
  color_data[0].width = (uint8_t)(results[g_max_color_column_index].box[2] - results[g_max_color_column_index].box[0]);
  color_data[0].length = (uint8_t)(results[g_max_color_column_index].box[3] - results[g_max_color_column_index].box[1]);
  break;
  1. task_process_handler() is the main task for color recognition. It registers thresholds to ColorDetector first, then continuously retrieves frames from the image queue, executes detection, draws the results back onto the image, and writes them to the result queue.
cpp
ColorDetector detector;
for (int i = 0; i < std_color_info.size(); ++i)
{
  detector.register_color(std_color_info[i].color_thresh, std_color_info[i].area_thresh, std_color_info[i].name);
}

if (xQueueReceive(xQueueFrameI, &frame, portMAX_DELAY))
{
  std::vector<std::vector<color_detect_result_t>> &results =
      detector.detect((uint16_t *)frame->buf, {(int)frame->height, (int)frame->width, 3});
}
  1. If a color is not detected in the current frame, the program actively clears the corresponding id, center point, and dimensions to prevent the main control from retrieving outdated data from the previous frame.
cpp
for(int i = 0; i < COLOR_NUM; ++i)
{
  if(results[i].size() == 0)
  {
    color_data[i].id = 0;
    color_data[i].center_x = 0;
    color_data[i].center_y = 0;
    color_data[i].width = 0;
    color_data[i].length = 0;
  }
}
  1. After the recognition task finishes, the program sends the image to the LCD for display, and also puts color_data into xQueueResult to be transmitted back to Tonybot by the I2C transmission module.
cpp
if (xQueueFrameO)
{
  xQueueSend(xQueueFrameO, &frame, portMAX_DELAY);
}
else if (gReturnFB)
{
  esp_camera_fb_return(frame);
}

if (xQueueResult)
{
  xQueueSend(xQueueResult, &color_data, portMAX_DELAY);
}
  1. register_color_detection is the external registration entry. It saves the input and output queues to global variables and then creates the color recognition task.
cpp
void register_color_detection(const QueueHandle_t frame_i,
                                   const QueueHandle_t event,
                                   const QueueHandle_t result,
                                   const QueueHandle_t frame_o,
                                   const bool camera_fb_return)
{
  xQueueFrameI = frame_i;
  xQueueFrameO = frame_o;
  xQueueEvent = event;
  xQueueResult = result;
  gReturnFB = camera_fb_return;

  xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(task_process_handler, TAG, 5 * 1024, NULL, 5, NULL, 1);
}
  • Tonybot
  1. main.py initializes Tonybot, the local I2C bus, the RGB ultrasonic sensor, and the machine.I2C used for communication with the module, where the module address is fixed to 0x51.
python
import Hiwonder
import Hiwonder_IIC
import machine
import time

iic = Hiwonder_IIC.IIC()
tony = Hiwonder.Tonybot()
sonar = Hiwonder_IIC.I2CSonar(iic)
sonar.setRGB(0, 0, 0, 0)

i2c = machine.I2C(0, scl=machine.Pin(23), sda=machine.Pin(22), freq=100000)
CAMERA_ADDR = 0x51
  1. After powering on, the robot returns to the default posture first, turns the head straight ahead, and then waits for the module and the expansion board to finish initialization.
python
tony.runActionGroup(0, 1)
tony.attachHead()
tony.moveHeadAngle(90)
time.sleep(0.2)
tony.detachHead()

time.sleep(2)
print("start.")
  1. To prevent the color recognition from flickering, the program adds three state variables HOLD_TIME, last_color, and last_seen_time to keep the LED lit for a short period.
python
HOLD_TIME = 1.0
last_color = None
last_seen_time = 0
  1. color_detection reads a 4-byte color result from register 0x04 each time. If the first byte contains abnormal values such as 163 or 255, the current data is discarded.
python
data = i2c.readfrom_mem(CAMERA_ADDR, 0x04, 4)

if data[0] in (163, 255):
    return
  1. The program then determines whether red, green, or blue is recognized based on the 4-byte return value, and updates the timestamp when the color was last seen.
python
found_color = None

if data[0] == 1:
    found_color = 1
elif data[1] == 2:
    found_color = 2
elif data[2] == 3:
    found_color = 3

if found_color is not None:
    last_color = found_color
    last_seen_time = now
  1. Within the HOLD_TIME window, even if the color is not recognized in one or two frames, the program maintains the previous LED color to reduce flickering.
python
if last_color is not None and (now - last_seen_time) <= HOLD_TIME:
    if last_color == 1:
        sonar.setRGB(0 , 255 , 0 , 0)
    elif last_color == 2:
        sonar.setRGB(0 , 0 , 255 , 0)
    elif last_color == 3:
        sonar.setRGB(0 , 0 , 0 , 255)
else:
    sonar.setRGB(0, 0, 0, 0)
    last_color = None
  1. The main loop calls color_detection continuously and refreshes every 0.05 seconds, balancing the recognition response speed and the I2C bus load.
python
def loop():
    while True:
        color_detection()
        time.sleep(0.05)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    loop()

6.8.6 Face Recognition ​

6.8.6.1 Project Introduction ​

This section introduces how to recognize whether a face is in front of the lens by connecting to the large AI model module on the chest of Tonybot. When a face is detected in front of the lens, the robot executes a waving action group.

6.8.6.2 Program Download ​

Refer to 6.8.3 Program Download of this chapter to learn how to download the program.

6.8.6.3 Program Outcome ​

When a face is detected in front of the lens of the large AI model module, Tonybot will execute the waving action group.

6.8.6.4 Program Analysis ​

  • Large AI Model Module
  1. face_detection.ino imports the camera, face detection, LCD, and I2C transmission modules first. The entire face recognition process is connected through these parts.
cpp
#include "camera_setting.h"
#include "face_detection.hpp"
#include "lcd_display.h"
#include "iic_data_send.hpp"
#include "arduino.h"
  1. Three sets of queues are similarly defined in the program to store raw images, drawn images, and face result data.
cpp
static QueueHandle_t xQueueAIFrame = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueLCDFrame = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueIICData = NULL;
  1. In setup, queues are created, and the camera, face detection, LCD, and I2C transmission modules are registered in sequence, forming a complete pipeline for image acquisition, detection, and transmission.
cpp
xQueueAIFrame = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
xQueueLCDFrame = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
xQueueIICData = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(target_face_information_t));

register_camera(PIXFORMAT_RGB565, 4, xQueueAIFrame);
register_human_face_detection(xQueueAIFrame, NULL, xQueueIICData, xQueueLCDFrame, false);
register_lcd_display(xQueueLCDFrame, NULL, NULL, NULL, true);
register_iic_data_send(xQueueIICData, NULL);
  1. Two-stage face models are imported in face_detection.cpp, and detect_result is defined to save the latest face center point and size information.
cpp
#include "face_detection.hpp"
#include "human_face_detect_msr01.hpp"
#include "human_face_detect_mnp01.hpp"

#define TWO_STAGE_ON 1

static QueueHandle_t xQueueFrameI = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueFrameO = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueResult = NULL;

static target_face_information_t detect_result;
  1. save_detection_result converts the bounding box output by the model into a center point, width, and length, and writes them into detect_result for subsequent transmission to the main control via the I2C bus.
cpp
if(prediction->keypoint.size() == 10)
{
  detect_result.center_x = (uint8_t)(prediction->box[0] + ((prediction->box[2] - prediction->box[0]) / 2));
  detect_result.center_y = (uint8_t)(prediction->box[1] + ((prediction->box[3] - prediction->box[1]) / 2));
  detect_result.width = (uint8_t)(prediction->box[2] - prediction->box[0]);
  detect_result.length = (uint8_t)(prediction->box[3] - prediction->box[1]);
}
  1. task_process_handler() is the main task for face recognition. It first calls HumanFaceDetectMSR01 to perform the first-stage candidate region detection, and then calls HumanFaceDetectMNP01 to perform the second-stage fine screening.
cpp
HumanFaceDetectMSR01 detector(0.3F, 0.3F, 10, 0.3F);
#if TWO_STAGE_ON
HumanFaceDetectMNP01 detector2(0.4F, 0.3F, 10);
#endif

std::list<dl::detect::result_t> &detect_candidates =
    detector.infer((uint16_t *)frame->buf, {(int)frame->height, (int)frame->width, 3});
std::list<dl::detect::result_t> &detect_results =
    detector2.infer((uint16_t *)frame->buf, {(int)frame->height, (int)frame->width, 3}, detect_candidates);
  1. If a face is detected in the current frame, the program draws a bounding box on the image and updates the result. If no face is detected, the center point and size are cleared.
cpp
if (detect_results.size() > 0)
{
  draw_detection_result((uint16_t *)frame->buf, frame->height, frame->width, detect_results);
  save_detection_result(detect_results);
}
else
{
  detect_result.center_x = 0;
  detect_result.center_y = 0;
  detect_result.width = 0;
  detect_result.length = 0;
}
  1. After the recognition process completes, the program sends the image to the LCD for display and also puts detect_result into the result queue for the I2C module to transmit to Tonybot.
cpp
if (xQueueFrameO)
{
  xQueueSend(xQueueFrameO, &frame, portMAX_DELAY);
}
else if (gReturnFB)
{
  esp_camera_fb_return(frame);
}

if (xQueueResult)
{
  xQueueSend(xQueueResult, &detect_result, portMAX_DELAY);
}
  1. register_human_face_detection is responsible for saving the queue handles and creating the background face recognition task.
cpp
void register_human_face_detection(const QueueHandle_t frame_i,
                                   const QueueHandle_t event,
                                   const QueueHandle_t result,
                                   const QueueHandle_t frame_o,
                                   const bool camera_fb_return)
{
    xQueueFrameI = frame_i;
    xQueueFrameO = frame_o;
    xQueueEvent = event;
    xQueueResult = result;
    gReturnFB = camera_fb_return;

    xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(task_process_handler, TAG, 5 * 1024, NULL, 2, NULL, 1);
}
  • Tonybot
  1. main.py initializes Tonybot, the local I2C bus, the RGB ultrasonic sensor, and the machine.I2C interface used for communication with the large AI model module.
python
import Hiwonder
import Hiwonder_IIC
import time
import machine

iic = Hiwonder_IIC.IIC()
tony = Hiwonder.Tonybot()
sonar = Hiwonder_IIC.I2CSonar(iic)
sonar.setRGB(0, 0, 0, 0)

i2c = machine.I2C(0, scl=machine.Pin(23), sda=machine.Pin(22), freq=100000)
CAMERA_ADDR = 0x51
  1. After startup, the robot executes action group 0 first to return to the default posture, and then turns the head straight ahead, waiting for the recognition program to stabilize.
python
tony.runActionGroup(0, 1)
tony.attachHead()
tony.moveHeadAngle(90)
time.sleep(0.2)
tony.detachHead()

time.sleep(2)
print("start.")
  1. face_detection reads a 4-byte face result from register 0x01 each time. As long as the first byte is not 0, it indicates that a face is detected in the current screen.
python
def face_detection():
    try:
        data = i2c.readfrom_mem(CAMERA_ADDR, 0x01, 4)

        if data[0] != 0:
            tony.runActionGroup(9, 1)
            time.sleep(5)
    except OSError:
        pass
  1. Action group 9 is triggered here, representing the waving and greeting action of the robot. The subsequent time.sleep(5) is used to avoid duplicate actions being triggered during continuous recognition.
python
if data[0] != 0:
    tony.runActionGroup(9, 1)
    time.sleep(5)
  1. The main loop continuously polls the face result, checking whether a face appears in the current screen every 0.1 seconds.
python
def loop():
    while True:
        face_detection()
        time.sleep(0.1)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    loop()

6.8.7 QR Code Recognition ​

6.8.7.1 Project Introduction ​

This section introduces how to recognize whether a specified QR code is in front of the lens by connecting to the large AI model module. If it is detected, the robot will execute the corresponding action group.

6.8.7.2 Program Download ​

Refer to 6.8.3 Program Download of this chapter to learn how to download the program.

6.8.7.3 Program Outcome ​

When a specified QR code appears in front of the lens of the large AI model module on the chest of Tonybot, the robot will execute the corresponding action group.

  • Execute action group 17 named dance.
  • Execute action group 103 named gymnastics.

6.8.7.4 Program Analysis ​

  • Large AI Model Module
  1. The main file on the module side for QR code recognition is code_recognition.ino. It imports the camera, QR code recognition, I2C transmission, and global structure definitions first.
cpp
#include "camera_setting.h"
#include "code_recognition.hpp"
#include "lcd_display.h"
#include "iic_data_send.hpp"
#include "global.h"
  1. Three sets of queues are similarly prepared in the program to transfer raw images, display images, and QR code recognition results.
cpp
static QueueHandle_t xQueueAIFrame = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueLCDFrame = NULL;
static QueueHandle_t xQueueIICData = NULL;
  1. setup creates these queues first, and registers the camera, QR code recognition, and I2C transmission modules in sequence, forming a complete offline recognition link.
cpp
xQueueAIFrame = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
xQueueLCDFrame = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(camera_fb_t *));
xQueueIICData = xQueueCreate(2, sizeof(I2C_Data_t));

register_camera(PIXFORMAT_RGB565, 4, xQueueAIFrame);
register_code_recognition(xQueueAIFrame, NULL, xQueueIICData, xQueueLCDFrame, false);
register_iic_data_send(xQueueIICData, NULL);
  1. The I2C return structure I2C_Data_t is defined in global.h, storing both the string content and the string length.
cpp
#define MAX_STRING_LEN  20

typedef struct {
    char data[MAX_STRING_LEN];
    uint8_t datalen;
}I2C_Data_t;
  1. The component responsible for scanning codes in code_recognition.cpp is esp_code_scanner. Each time an image frame is received, the program creates the code scanner, configures the image format, and starts recognition.
cpp
esp_image_scanner_t *esp_scn = esp_code_scanner_create();
esp_code_scanner_config_t config = {
    ESP_CODE_SCANNER_MODE_FAST,
    ESP_CODE_SCANNER_IMAGE_RGB565,
    frame->width,
    frame->height
};
esp_code_scanner_set_config(esp_scn, config);
int decoded_num = esp_code_scanner_scan_image(esp_scn, frame->buf);
  1. If the recognition is successful, the program copies the QR code content into i2c_data.data and records datalen. If not detected, "null" is returned by default.
cpp
if(decoded_num){
    esp_code_scanner_symbol_t result = esp_code_scanner_result(esp_scn);
    strncpy(i2c_data.data, result.data, sizeof(i2c_data.data));
    i2c_data.datalen = result.datalen;
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(20));
}
else {
    strncpy(i2c_data.data, "null", sizeof(i2c_data.data));
    i2c_data.datalen = 5;
}
  1. After processing the current frame, the program destroys the code scanner, manages the image buffer, and sends the QR code recognition result to xQueueResult to be transmitted to the main control by the I2C module.
cpp
esp_code_scanner_destroy(esp_scn);

if (xQueueFrameO)
{
    xQueueSend(xQueueFrameO, &frame, portMAX_DELAY);
}
else if (gReturnFB)
{
    esp_camera_fb_return(frame);
}

if (xQueueResult)
{
  xQueueSend(xQueueResult, &i2c_data, portMAX_DELAY);
}
  1. register_code_recognition binds the queues and starts the QR code recognition task.
cpp
void register_code_recognition(const QueueHandle_t frame_i,
                                   const QueueHandle_t event,
                                   const QueueHandle_t result,
                                   const QueueHandle_t frame_o,
                                   const bool camera_fb_return)
{
  xQueueFrameI = frame_i;
  xQueueFrameO = frame_o;
  xQueueEvent = event;
  xQueueResult = result;
  gReturnFB = camera_fb_return;

  xTaskCreatePinnedToCore(task_process_handler, TAG, 5 * 1024, NULL, 2, NULL, 1);
}
  • Tonybot
  1. main.py initializes Tonybot, the local I2C bus, and the machine.I2C used for communication with the large AI model module. The QR code recognition results are also read through the address 0x51.
python
import Hiwonder
import Hiwonder_IIC
import time
import machine

iic = Hiwonder_IIC.IIC()
tony = Hiwonder.Tonybot()
sonar = Hiwonder_IIC.I2CSonar(iic)
sonar.setRGB(0, 0, 0, 0)

i2c = machine.I2C(0, scl=machine.Pin(23), sda=machine.Pin(22), freq=100000)
CAMERA_ADDR = 0x51
  1. After startup, the robot executes action group 0 first to restore its body posture and head direction to the uniform initial state.
python
tony.runActionGroup(0, 1)
tony.attachHead()
tony.moveHeadAngle(90)
time.sleep(0.2)
tony.detachHead()

time.sleep(2)
print("start.")
  1. code_detection reads 21 bytes of data from register 0x00 each time. The first byte is the string length, and the subsequent bytes are the actual QR code content.
python
data = i2c.readfrom_mem(CAMERA_ADDR, 0x00, 21)
length = data[0]

if 0 < length < 21:
    raw_val = data[1 : 1 + length].decode('utf-8', 'ignore').strip('\x00')
  1. After parsing the QR code content, the program decides which action group to execute based on the string content. Here, dance corresponds to action group 17, and gymnastics corresponds to action group 103.
python
if 'dance' in raw_val:
    tony.runActionGroup(17, 1)
    time.sleep(2)

elif 'gymnastics' in raw_val:
    tony.runActionGroup(103, 1)
    time.sleep(2)
  1. If the QR code content is null, it indicates that no valid target is currently recognized. The robot will remain in standby mode without executing any action.
python
elif 'null' in raw_val:
